details: Our project, developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, is an interactive digital educational platform designed to make space science more accessible, understandable, and engaging for everyone. Through a three-dimensional model of the Solar System, users will be able to explore the eight planets, their major moons, and other celestial bodies while gaining scientific knowledge about planetary structures, atmospheres, star formation, stellar life cycles, black holes, and constellations. One of the key features of our project, the **Digital Time Machine**, will allow users to compare scientific data and discoveries from different periods and examine how our understanding of space has evolved throughout history. Additionally, the Orbit Atlas section will focus on space debris surrounding Earth and its impact on space exploration, while the Space Exploration Archive will present significant space missions, spacecraft launches, and scientific advancements in chronological order. By combining scientific research, technology, and visual learning, our project aims to encourage users to explore the universe from both scientific and historical perspectives while fostering curiosity and interest in space science.
